items.title: Ada Rovatti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 13, 2022
items.q: Nobody would have thought about saying oh we have Stan Getz and da-da-da-da on it.

ctx.x: Wonderful. You know in a perfect world the idea of the woman jazz musician wouldn’t be an issue. Like you’re a jazz musician. But I guess we’re not at that point yet. Have you experienced not getting work that you thought you would have — how do I phrase this? Do you think you’ve lost work because you are a woman jazz musician?

Well I have mixed feelings about all these movements about you know women. Because yes we have been discriminated for a long time. But okay let’s start with the fact yes, we are still seen as kind of like, you know, the beard woman. The circus little gimmick. So, and you know, so festivals say, “Hey we already have a female saxophone player so we cannot hire you.” It’s like, “Yeah but you have 15 male saxophone players.” So sometimes we are still seen as something like a token. At the festivals they need to have…

for reviews, the same for a lot of things. Of course some counterpoints say yeah but you know a lot of times in private events they want a girl playing saxophone because it’s cool. Yeah but you know it’s just like it’s minimal. You know you still need to be able to perform you know. So you know, and all the other things it’s like on the other side just to kind of like I don’t know how to straight out the way I’m thinking you know. I found that sometimes you know there is a little too much fear of saying anything…
